international.title: Ed Miliband defends doing 2015 election interview with Russell Brand, saying he was ‘taking him on’ not endorsing him – UK politics live
international.summary: Ed Balls, shadow chancellor at the time, said he had warned Labour leader not to go ahead with ‘ridiculous’ interview Good morning. There are two issues that will dominate the political news this week – the EU reset, and the Alan Milburn report on youth unemployment – and this morning there are new lines on both of these issues. Andy Burnham has set out “three tests” for the deal that he is due to agree with the EU at a summit on Friday. Tonight he is giving the traditional prime ministerial speech to the lord mayor’s banquet in London, which by convention focuses on foreign policy, and, according to the overnight briefing from Downing Street, he will announce three tests. No 10 says: Ahead of this week’s UK-EU Summit, the prime minister will set out three tests for any agreement: -First, it must be consistent with the manifesto and the Government’s red lines. It’s like the Emperor’s new clothes – where no one is prepared to say the obvious truth. Well, I say it as I see it. And to be frank, the Emperor has nothing on. The Brexit we were given has not worked. We have lost more than we gained. Alan Milburn is expected to say that employer national insurance for workers under the age of 25 should be cut in his report published tomorrow, the BBC is reporting. Many of Milburn’s recommendations have already been made public, but this is new, and it is likely to be welcomed by Kemi Badenoch, who is holding a press conference later, because the Tories have repeatedly been saying that Rachel Reeves’s decision to raise employer national insurance has been bad for jobs.
